blocks.heading: S7900 Odd Form Insert Machine — automate the components no standard machine will touch

nodes.text: THT odd-form component automation
S7900 Odd Form Insert Machine — automate the components no standard machine will touch

Connectors, switches, transformer coils, ports and terminals: the S7900 series inserts odd-form components at 0.6–0.8 seconds each with 2 to 6 heads, ±0.05 mm vision accuracy and a full tape, tray, tube and bowl feeder ecosystem.
Five configurations — S7900-II / IV / IV-P / VI / VI-P — cover standalone cells through inline lines with lead clinching. Final configuration confirmed after technical review.

blocks.heading: Odd form is where THT lines quietly lose money

nodes.text: The hidden cost of manual odd-form insertion
Odd form is where THT lines quietly lose money
The parts your SMT line cannot place pile up on a manual bench — slow, inconsistent and impossible to staff at scale.
Odd form stays manual
Connectors, coils and terminals sit outside standard placement. They accumulate on a hand-insertion bench that grows with every new product.
Every new part is a new problem
Without flexible feeding, each odd shape demands new fixtures, new training and new excuses for slow starts.
Floaters at the wave
Hand-inserted parts lift and shift during soldering. Floaters and tombstones are rework you pay for twice.
Mixed boards need mixed feeding
Real boards mix connectors, coils, terminals and clips. One feeder type never covers the BOM, so half the parts stay manual.
The bench sets line pace
Mounters run at machine speed while boards wait at odd-form hand stations. Throughput is capped by fingers, not motors.
Audit and traceability gaps
Manual steps leave no record. Customers auditing traceability see a gap exactly where your risk lives.

nodes.q: What components can the S7900 insert?
nodes.a: Connectors, switches, sockets, transformer coils, ports, capacitors, resistors, ICs and terminals — up to Ø50 (35×35 mm) body size and 20–30 mm height depending on variant. Insertion force is available up to 98 N on the S7900-IV for tight press-fit parts.

nodes.q: How do you handle our special odd-form parts?
nodes.a: Send samples or drawings. Southern Machinery designs customized grippers and nozzles in-house — the same tooling capability behind our customized SMT nozzles — so parts without a standard pickup get a dedicated one.

Radial and axial tape feeders including a 90° bending version, programmable tray feeders, tube feeders (including vibration and stacked types) and customized bowl feeders, up to 20 stations per machine. Mixed feeder types on one machine are supported.
Yes — automatic lead clinching is standard on the S7900-IV-P and optional on the S7900-VI-P, with outward, inner, circular and two-turn bending modes for leads under 1.0 mm.

nodes.q: Can it run inline with MES?
nodes.a: Yes. MES connection is standard configuration. The machine supports inline operation with PCB loading and unloading, chain or belt conveyors, left-to-right or right-to-left flow, and automatic conveyor adjustment.

nodes.q: How do I get a price and delivery time?
nodes.a: Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your component samples or drawings, board sizes and monthly volume. Feasibility, configuration and quotation are provided after technical confirmation — typically within 24 hours.
